readout_other: whole-cell patch clamp recordings of spontaneous action potentials and voltage-dependent potassium currents (IA, IK) in CA1 pyramidal neurons
direction_notes: US increased spontaneous firing rate and action potential amplitude while inhibiting transient outward (IA) and delayed rectifier (IK) potassium currents, shifting their voltage dependence and slowing IA recovery from inactivation.

exposures.label: Ultrasonic stimulation of hippocampal CA1 brain slices

timing.protocol_description: The ultrasound settings were 0.5 MHz center frequency, 20 Hz pulse repetition frequency, 50% duty cycle and 20 ms pulse length, and the pulse-average ultrasound intensities were 15 mW/cm2 or 30 mW/cm2. All stimulations lasted 15 min. The transducer (diameter 24 mm) was immersed in aCSF 1.5 cm above the brain slice and stimulated the entire slice.

source_quotes.n_subjects: The number of rats for each control and experimental group is 12 $( \boldsymbol { \mathrm { n } } = 1 2 )$ Four brain slices of each rat were used for control and experimental groups.

flags.reason: Control condition was brain slices with no stimulation applied; the paper does not describe whether an inactive transducer was left in place, so the sham mechanism is not fully described.
Stated pulse length (20 ms) does not exactly match duty_cycle/PRF (50%/20 Hz = 25 ms); recorded as stated, not corrected.
Paper reports 'pulse-average ultrasound intensity' without stating whether this was measured in water/free field or at the slice; placed in unspecified_domain.
Paper does not state whether patch-clamp recordings were made during or after the 15-minute ultrasound exposure.
